items.reason: The video states that John executed many of the surrendered noble defenders at Rochester Castle, when in fact only one crossbowman was executed and the rest were imprisoned, which directly impacts mark schemes.

mark_affecting.quote: instead of showing customary chivalric mercy to the surrendered noble defenders, John executed many of them.

items.subject: history-edexcel
items.title: Manifest Destiny and the Pull of the West
items.reason: The video incorrectly places the Sierra Nevada on the Oregon Trail, misattributing key geography examined in the specification.

mark_affecting.quote: They had to cross the high mountain passes of the Sierra Nevada before the heavy winter snows hit

items.subject: history-edexcel
items.title: Cattle's End, the Range Wars and Frontier Law and Order
items.reason: The video states that the Johnson County invaders were tried by a packed jury and acquitted, whereas the case never reached a jury and charges were dropped due to prosecution costs.

mark_affecting.quote: Back in court, the cattle barons packed the jury with friendly faces they'd paid for, and every single defendant was acquitted. (Also on slide at 05:32: 'Cavalry saves gunmen, jury acquits')

items.subject: history-edexcel
items.title: The Atlantic Economy: Trade, Tobacco and Piracy
items.reason: The video explicitly claims both on screen and in narration that the Piracy Act 1717 established colonial vice-admiralty courts and ended the requirement to ship pirates to London, directly contradicting the corrected facts and misattributing the powers granted under the 1698 Act.

mark_affecting.quote: 1717: Piracy Act establishes colonial courts. [...] Before the 1717 Piracy Act, if you caught a pirate you had to ship them all the way back across the Atlantic to London for a trial. [...] These new courts allowed pirates to be tried quickly, right there on-site in the colonies.

items.subject: history-edexcel
items.title: The Great Awakening and the Enlightenment
items.reason: The video states and illustrates that newspapers grew to over 40 by the 1760s (F8), which teaches the wrong figure and would lead to incorrect answers on lesson assessments.

mark_affecting.quote: Fast forward to the 1760s, there were over 40 of them.

items.subject: history-edexcel
items.title: After Victory: Frontier and Tax Tensions, 1763–64
items.reason: The video states that General Amherst directly ordered the distribution of smallpox blankets (contradicting the corrected lesson text where the garrison acted independently) and falsely attributes the quotation 'taxation without representation is tyranny' to James Otis's 1764 pamphlet.

mark_affecting.quote: General Amherst himself ordered the distribution of smallpox-infected blankets to Indigenous warriors.
a lawyer named James Otis published a pamphlet objecting to the Act, and it gave us this totally iconic quote: 'Taxation without representation is tyranny.'

items.subject: history-edexcel
items.title: The End of the Mandate and the Creation of Israel, 1945–48
items.reason: The video presents Operation Agatha as a consequence rather than the trigger of the King David Hotel bombing, reversing key cause-and-effect chronology.

mark_affecting.quote: Immediately following the attack, the British launched Operation Agatha, arresting around 2,700 Jewish suspects.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Economy, society and the Nazi winners and losers
items.reason: F22 is mark-affecting because the video teaches that the Reich Mother's Cross was introduced in 1933 instead of December 1938, giving students the wrong date for a key examined Nazi social policy.

mark_affecting.quote: They took it so seriously, they even introduced the Reich Mother's Cross in 1933, literally handing out bronze, silver and gold medals to women

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Women, education and the One Child Policy
items.reason: The video incorrectly attributes explicit domestic violence protections to the 1980 Marriage Law, which were not enacted until 2001 and would be marked as factually inaccurate on an exam.

mark_affecting.quote: It strengthened divorce proceedings and offered explicit protections against domestic violence

items.subject: history-edexcel
items.title: Spain in 1490: Crusading Spirit and Foreign Ambitions
items.reason: F2 is mark_affecting because the video states Torquemada led the Inquisition upon its founding in 1478 and incorrectly defines conversos as including Muslim converts, which directly contradicts the lesson definition and mark scheme.

mark_affecting.quote: they founded the Spanish Inquisition in 1478, led by Tomás de Torquemada. Their main target at this time was a group called the conversos. These were Jews and Muslims who had converted to Christianity.

items.subject: history-edexcel
items.title: The Conquistadors Begin: Balboa, Cuba and Magellan
items.reason: The video and slide state that Magellan's Pacific crossing took '99 weeks' rather than 99 days, presenting an impossible timeline that contradicts the 1519–1522 duration of the voyage.

mark_affecting.quote: brutal 99-week Pacific crossing (and on-screen text '99 Weeks' at 06:32)

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: The Roaring Twenties and Republican prosperity
items.reason: The video gives the wrong date for the Fordney-McCumber Tariff (1921 instead of 1922), which can cost students marks on exam questions.

mark_affecting.quote: the Fordney-McCumber Tariff of 1921 slapped high taxes on foreign goods

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Reactions to the New Deal
items.reason: The video explicitly states and visually features the incorrect $3 million cap on personal fortunes instead of the corrected $50 million figure from Huey Long's Share Our Wealth plan.

mark_affecting.quote: To put a hard cap on personal fortunes at exactly 3 million dollars.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Native Americans, Chicanos and other civil rights movements
items.reason: The video incorrectly states that Russell Means founded AIM alongside Dennis Banks in 1968, teaching a wrong fact regarding AIM's founders.

mark_affecting.quote: It was founded in 1968 in Minneapolis by Dennis Banks and Russell Means.

items.title: NATO, Warsaw Pact and the Berlin Wall
items.reason: The video explicitly centers an entire hook and recurring figure around '9 days' between West Germany joining NATO and the Warsaw Pact being signed, when the correct interval tested in the lesson is 5 days.

mark_affecting.quote: just think about this number: 9. It was exactly nine days between West Germany officially joining the Western military alliance, and the Soviet Union firing back with their own massive counter-treaty.
It was exactly nine days between West Germany officially joining the Western military alliance, and the Soviet Union firing back with their own massive counter-treaty. Nine days.
So, as we saw with that number nine earlier, Moscow reacted instantly.
just think about this number: 9. It was exactly nine days
just think about this number: 9. It was exactly nine days

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: End of the war and its international legacy
items.reason: The video teaches students the non-existent 'Popular Majority' school of appeasement historiography and mislabels R.A.C. Parker as a revisionist, which would cost marks on an interpretations question.

mark_affecting.quote: Second, the popular majority view in 1961 argued appeasement just reflected a genuine public desire to avoid war... Finally, the Parker revisionist view argues...

items.subject: history-edexcel
items.title: The Red Guards and the Red Terror, 1966-68
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims that Liu Shaoqi was publicly paraded in a dunce cap at a university rally (which was actually his wife Wang Guangmei at Tsinghua University), causing students to fail lesson checks on the leadership purges.

mark_affecting.quote: The president himself, Liu Shaoqi, was publicly paraded in a dunce cap at a university rally.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Soweto Uprising and youth resistance
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims on slide and in voiceover that the Soweto Students' Representative Council (SSRC) was active pre-1976, when in fact it was formed in August 1976 after the uprising began.

mark_affecting.quote: SSRC active pre-1976 / Groups like the Soweto Students' Representative Council had actually been highly active long before June 1976.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Election 1994 and the new South Africa
items.reason: The video incorrectly states that a 20 percent vote threshold was required for cabinet representation (which was actually 5 percent, while 20 percent was the threshold for an Executive Deputy President), directly affecting marks on questions testing the Government of National Unity rules.

mark_affecting.quote: The key rule here was that any party winning over 20 percent of the vote was automatically entitled to representation in the cabinet.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Anglo-Saxon kingship c.1000-1066
items.reason: The narration mistakenly states '10,000 AD' instead of '1000 AD' at 00:19, giving students an incorrect date that would cost marks on an exam.

mark_affecting.video_says: by around the year 10,000 AD, England wasn't just a fractured set of squabbling territories anymore
mark_affecting.lesson_says: By around 1000 AD, England had developed into a single, unified kingdom under the House of Wessex.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: State, war and welfare 1914-1979
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims that DORA was used to conscript men into the armed forces (F26), when conscription was actually introduced separately under the Military Service Act of 1916.

mark_affecting.quote: And ultimately, they used DORA to conscript men into the armed forces.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Jews in medieval England 1066-1290
items.reason: The video includes the inaccurate claim that Henry III debunked blood libel and jailed accusers, directly contradicting historical fact.

mark_affecting.quote: King Henry III once investigated a blood libel claim, found it to be total nonsense, and actually threw the Christian accusers in prison

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Africans, Asians and other migrants in early modern England
items.reason: The video prominently dates Reasonable Blackman to 1507 (on timeline, slide, and narration), misdating an Elizabethan craftsman by 70 years and before English parish records even existed.

mark_affecting.quote: 1507 Reasonable Blackman active in London [and at 03:50: 'working in Southwark around 1507']

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Two world wars and inter-war migration
items.reason: The video incorrectly states that Charles Wootton drowned in Cardiff rather than Liverpool, which would lose marks on a question examining the 1919 port riots.

mark_affecting.quote: In Cardiff, it tragically led to the drowning of a Black man named Charles Wootton while he was trying to escape a mob.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Commonwealth migration after 1945
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims the British Nationality Act was passed weeks before the Windrush arrived (F10) and attributes the concept of patriality and making passport holders stateless to the 1968 Act (F13), both of which teach incorrect legal definitions and historical chronology.

mark_affecting.quote: Just weeks before the Windrush arrived, the government passed the 1948 British Nationality Act. Basically, this act confirmed that all Commonwealth subjects were officially British citizens.
a crucial exam term that was introduced by that 1968 Act, and that's patriality... the 1968 Act effectively made them stateless overnight.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Ideas of Englishness and Britishness over time
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims Norman migrants assimilated rapidly within a few generations and anglicised their names, which misteaches a key medieval case study on change and continuity.

mark_affecting.quote: Groups from your early lessons, like the Norman migrants or the Huguenot refugees, assimilated quite rapidly. Within a few generations, they anglicised their names and dissolved completely into English society.

items.subject: geography-eduqas
items.title: Presenting & Analysing Fieldwork
items.reason: The video states both visually and aloud that the slope of a line of best fit reveals the strength of the relationship, which is a known GCSE correlation misconception that loses marks in an analysis question.

mark_affecting.quote: The slope of this line instantly reveals the strength of the relationship between your variables.

items.subject: geography-eduqas
items.title: Conclusions, Evaluation & UK Decisions
items.reason: The video incorrectly advises students that using a metre rule instead of a tape measure is a top-mark improvement to reduce tape stretch, which is an invalid methodology that would lose marks in an exam evaluation question.

mark_affecting.quote: A strong, maximum mark improvement is saying something like: use a metre rule rather than a tape measure to completely reduce stretch error.

items.subject: history-edexcel
items.title: Brest-Litovsk and the Civil War, 1918–21
items.reason: The video prominently features and narrates incorrect headline statistics for Brest-Litovsk (25% of population and 25% of industry instead of 34% and 54%), which would teach students inaccurate historical figures on an examined specification topic.

mark_affecting.quote: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk cost Russia a staggering 25% of its entire population... another 25% of its entire industry... they lost almost half, 50% of their grain-producing land

items.subject: history-edexcel
items.title: The Five-Year Plans and Soviet Industry
items.reason: The video incorrectly dates Stalin's famous '50 or 100 years behind' speech to 1927 rather than February 1931, presenting it as a pre-plan justification rather than an address three years into the First Five-Year Plan.

mark_affecting.quote: In 1927 Stalin famously declared, 'We are 50 or 100 years behind the advanced countries...'

items.subject: geography-eduqas
items.title: Vulnerability & Reducing Tectonic Risk
items.reason: F8 is mark-affecting because claiming vertical evacuation towers are built inland contradicts the core geographical rationale that they are built within low-lying inundation zones specifically because people lack the time to evacuate inland.

mark_affecting.quote: In tsunami zones, they build vertical evacuation towers inland, so people actually have somewhere safe to run.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Norman conquest and feudal warfare 1066-1215
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims on screen and in audio that King John lost Normandy at the Battle of Bouvines in 1214, when Normandy was lost in 1204 and Bouvines merely ended his attempt to regain it.

mark_affecting.quote: He lost the ancestral lands of Normandy at the Battle of Bouvines in 1214.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Elizabeth, Spain and the new world
items.reason: The video incorrectly locates the fireship attack at Gravelines instead of Calais and claims storms wrecked two-thirds of the fleet (contradicting the actual loss of around 50 of 130 ships), both of which are mark-affecting errors for GCSE students.

mark_affecting.quote: Fireships at Gravelines caused panic. / when the Spanish eventually anchored at Gravelines, the English sent in burning fireships
Severe storms wrecked two-thirds of the fleet. / storms that wrecked roughly two-thirds of their entire fleet

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Border warfare c.1500-c.1600
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims Henry VIII was fighting in Italy against the French in 1513, which would cause a student to lose marks when explaining the strategic context of the Auld Alliance and the causes of the Battle of Flodden.

mark_affecting.quote: That was triggered exactly because Henry VIII was busy fighting in Italy against the French

items.subject: geography-eduqas
items.title: Social Challenges in Africa & South Asia
items.reason: The video states and displays an incorrect infant mortality rate of 27 per 1,000 for sub-Saharan Africa (which is actually around 48 per 1,000, 27 being near the world average).

mark_affecting.quote: In sub-Saharan Africa, around 27 babies in every 1,000 die before their first birthday

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Ireland 1688-1691 and the Jacobite threat
items.reason: Calling the departure of the Wild Geese a 'forced emigration' conflates migration categories (voluntary/agreed exile vs. forced emigration) that GCSE Empire and Migration specifications explicitly assess.

mark_affecting.quote: This was an absolutely massive forced emigration.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Bank of England, East India Company and the trade revolution
items.reason: The video presents incorrect dates for the Calico Acts (1690 and 1720 instead of 1700 and 1721) and falsely claims Parliament renewed the East India Company's monopoly in 1700 when Parliament actually broke it in 1698.

mark_affecting.quote: This direct pressure led to the Calico Acts of 1690 and 1720.
And by 1700, Parliament had officially renewed their royal monopoly on Asian trade.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Consumerism, coffee houses and political activism
items.reason: The video presents Mary Astell as an anti-slavery writer and places Olaudah Equiano within the 1688–c.1730 period, both of which would cause students to lose marks for citing incorrect or out-of-period evidence.

mark_affecting.quote: writers like Mary Astell started pointing out the glaring hypocrisy of it all, like how could a nation constantly celebrate its own liberty while actively enslaving others?
someone who truly embodies the wild contradictions of this whole era is Olaudah Equiano... his early life directly crossed paths with this exact same coffee-house world we've been talking about

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Spitalfields: site introduction and Huguenot weavers
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims that the Huguenot community built Christ Church Spitalfields as a statement of their prosperity, when it was actually commissioned and funded by Parliament under the 1711 Act to assert the Anglican Church over foreign Protestants.

mark_affecting.quote: Building this incredible structure and actually converting to Anglicanism was a huge statement. It proved their prosperity

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Kenilworth Castle: location and physical fabric
items.reason: The video incorrectly attributes the creation of the Great Mere to 'the castle's owners in the 1240s' rather than King John between 1210 and 1216, teaching an inaccurate date and patron on a core specification key fact.

mark_affecting.quote: In the 1240s, the castle's owners did something incredibly ambitious: they actually dammed the local streams... to create what's known as the Great Mere.

items.subject: history-ocr
items.title: Kenilworth's functions: defence, residence, administration
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims Henry III took formal possession in 1244 (he granted it away to Simon de Montfort) and wrongly states Simon de Montfort the Younger was defeated at Evesham.

mark_affecting.quote: In fact, in 1244, Henry III took formal possession of it, simply because he recognised just how strategically vital this spot was
In 1266, following the defeat of the rebel Simon de Montfort the Younger, his surviving supporters actually retreated to Kenilworth.
